Cards of Bellum is a War-inspired roguelike deck builder. Lead your poor army of rebels, unlock powerful heroes, counter suits, and unleash spells in your quest to overthrow the evil king and claim victory.

LEAD RULE-BREAKING HEROES

• Wizards duel by elemental mastery (Fire beats Death, Water beats Fire)

• Assassins strike randomly from the shadows

• Kings can reverse defeat

• Thieves steal your opponent's best cards, or a named hero unleashes special abilities

Use your cards wisely — a wasted hero can mean the difference between victory and defeat.

MASTER SUITED COMBAT

Swords beat Spears. Spears beat Horse. Horse beats Shields. Shields beat Swords. But when strength is close, roll the dice and a lucky 4 could save you.

SHAPE YOUR ADVENTURE

As you progress across the map, unique events will shape your journey. Choose wisely, as past decisions can trigger future events..

60+ UNIQUE CARDS

From numbered troops to Knights, Queens, Kings, Wizards, Thieves, and more. Build your strategy. Find your combos. Claim victory.

The throne awaits. So does the axe.

Short battles. Subtle decisions. Big consequences.


Cardume is a real-time 1v1 card battler. Two swarms of thousands of living cells fight in a glowing arena. Steer yours with a handful of cards. Lure the swarm onto a point, rally it into a charge, trigger a gorge, freeze an enemy assault. You can't micromanage individual cells, but a few well-timed plays ripple through thousands of them and swing the whole match.

Emergent warfare


Your cells obey simple rules, and thousands of them together turn those rules into a war. Learn to read the swarm so you can anticipate your enemy and tip the balance of the medium in your favor.

Win two ways


  • Domination: hold the arena's richest nutrient points and race to the victory-point goal.

  • Conversion: assimilate the enemy until their swarm collapses.

Lean defensive and hold the map and your cards, or go for the throat. Acid trails, cryo blasts, spore clouds, membranes. Every card reshapes the living system in real time.

Modes


  • Draft: open boosters, build a deck on the fly, and run it as far as you can, ranked against humans or against bots on your own.

  • Constructed: bring your own preconfigured swarm into the ladder.

  • Challenges: a hand-built ladder that teaches one idea at a time.

  • Auto-battler: prefer to just watch? Configure a swarm, set it loose hands-off, and let it fight rival swarms on its own.

A living, luminous arena

Abstract, bioluminescent, faintly psychedelic. Cardume is built to be mesmerizing to watch as much as to play. Light, motion, and emergent life.

PACK THE HOLD. PICK YOUR FACTIONS. TRY NOT TO DIE.

Every run starts the same: an empty cargo grid, three faction stations, and a delivery contract that could go very wrong.
The legal cargo pays. The illegal cargo pays more. The unknown cargo pays the most — if it doesn't mutate before you reach a buyer.

By sector three, you're hauling contraband through a Federation blockade with one shield bank left, a pirate squadron on your tail, and a boss between you and the warp gate. You either extract clean or you lose the run.

▸ TETRIS YOUR CARGO, DODGE INSPECTIONS
Pack your hold by hand. Safe slots up top, risk slots below. Federation scanners read top-to-bottom — what you stash where decides whether you make the next station or get boarded.

▸ THREE FACTIONS, NO FRIENDS
Federation, Pirates, Swine. Each pays differently, hates someone else, and remembers what you did last run. Working both sides is the highest paycheck and the fastest way to get hunted.

▸ EVERY SYSTEM IS A TRADEOFF
Power between shields, weapons, and engines mid-fight. Heat from contraband draws patrols. Mutating cargo can spike or crash in value before you dock. Nothing is free.

▸ NINE SHIPS, BRANCHING UPGRADES
Each ship sets your base hold shape, slot ratio, and special ability. Stack boon synergies between runs to make your loadout
do something none of the others can.

▸ BOSS EVERY SECTOR
Sector-ending encounters that punish whatever build you've been getting away with. If you only know one strategy, you'll learn three more or die trying.

▸ PERMADEATH, PERSISTENT META
Lose a run, keep your weapons stash and meta upgrades. Each death pushes the next attempt further.

DAILY SEEDED RUNS + GLOBAL LEADERBOARDS
Same conditions for everyone. Your scoreboard against theirs.

The grill's hot, the lights are on, and there's already a line. One hot dog stand on the carnival midway, and a crowd that's hungry right now.

Work the Grill

Hotdogs on the grill. Buns on to warm. Grab the right container, add ketchup or mustard if they asked for it, and get it over the counter while it's still hot.

Feed the Line

They just keep coming. Families, kids, couples, the whole fair getting hungry at the same time. Get on a roll and it feels incredible.

Don't Run Dry

Buns, hotdogs, boxes. It all comes in by the crate and it all comes out of your pocket. Sell out before the evening rush and you'll stand there watching the money walk straight past you.

Earn the Good Stuff

You start with hot dogs. Nothing else. Work your way up to pizza by the slice, donuts by the box, ice-cold soda on a hot night, and watch a whole new crowd turn up at your counter.

One More Day

The carousel spins, the ferris wheel turns, the string lights come on over your counter. Every morning brings a fresh crowd and another shot at beating yesterday's run.

MAKE FILTHY CARPETS CLEAN AGAIN

Carpet Daddy is a first-person carpet cleaning simulator built around satisfying transformations. Take on cleaning contracts, work through the mess with professional tools, and reveal a fresh carpet one careful pass at a time.

Assess the room, move furniture out of the way, and choose the right treatment for the dirt in front of you. Different messes need different tools, so a great result starts before the extractor touches the carpet.

USE THE RIGHT TOOL FOR THE JOB

  • Vacuum loose debris to prepare the carpet.

  • Pre-spray dirty areas before the deeper clean.

  • Agitate the carpet fibres to work treatment into stubborn dirt.

  • Spot-treat stains that need extra attention.

  • Extract dirt and cleaning solution to reveal the clean surface underneath.

WORK THE WHOLE ROOM

The dirt does not stop at the edge of the sofa. Move furniture, reach awkward corners, and work across the room until the carpet is properly clean. Watch the contrast grow between the mess you arrived to and the clean stripes left by each pass.

COMPLETE CONTRACTS AND RETURN TO YOUR WORKSHOP

Take on jobs with different rooms, layouts and cleaning challenges. Finish the work, earn payment and reviews, then return to your workshop to prepare for the next contract.

ENJOY THE PROCESS

Find the dirty spots, choose your tools, and settle into the sounds and rhythm of cleaning. The reward is a room you can look back on and see how much has changed.

Wishlist Carpet Daddy to follow development and hear when the full game is ready.

Hide It or Find It! 🔍

Carry Bros: Find It Together is a fast-paced online multiplayer party game where the Red Team and Blue Team compete across industrial locations filled with machinery, containers, warehouses, and hidden corners.

At the start of each round, one team becomes the Hiders and the other becomes the Seekers.

📦 Hiders receive random objects and must hide them naturally around the map before time runs out. Change their color, reduce the search timer, freeze opponents, or limit their vision.

🔍 Seekers must explore every corner and find all hidden objects. Collect random power-ups such as extra time, increased speed, a Hot & Cold Scanner, and an X-Ray Scan.

5 Industrial Maps 🏭

Explore five handcrafted maps filled with machinery, pipes, containers, storage rooms, and countless hiding places. Learn each location and use the environment to outsmart your opponents.

While waiting in the interactive lobby, play football or search bonus boxes for useful power-ups.

Random roles, objects, maps, abilities, and bonuses make every match different. Team up with your friends, develop your strategy, and complete your objective before the timer reaches zero!

Live the life of a footballer — from your own room, a cork board and a second-division shirt, to the biggest nights in Europe. And play every single match with cards.

EVERY MATCH IS A HAND OF CARDS

No simulation slider, no auto-play. On matchday you sit at the table:

  • Draw from your own deck and build poker hands — pairs, straights, flushes. CHIPS × MULT decides the strength of every move.

  • Your opponent plays real hands from their own deck. Every move pushes a tug-of-war bar: push it far enough and it's a GOAL — let them push back and the away end goes quiet.

  • Four suits shape how you score: POWER, STRIKE, FLAIR and PASS. Strike-heavy hands finish chances, pass-built goals become assists, physical hands break the opponent's move in half.

  • Eight hands per match and a handful of swaps — spend them like they're minutes on the clock.

  • Two-legged European nights, and when it all ends level: penalty shootouts, card against card.

YOUR DECK IS YOUR CAREER

  • One deck follows you through your entire career.

  • Upgrade single cards with stamps — lucky, golden, steel, glass, extra chips, extra mult.

  • Level up your hands until a humble Pair hits like a Straight.

  • Your player's skills unlock deck upgrades: development doesn't inflate numbers, it opens doors.

BUILD YOUR JOKER TABLE

  • 40 jokers across three rarity tiers, each bending the rules of the match in its own way.

  • Up to five on your table, all active, all stacking. Some sign short contracts and walk away — keep your table alive.

  • Chips are the only currency, and only playing earns them. Spend them in the magazine on your desk: jokers, card packs, hand upgrades, season vouchers.

A CAREER THAT FEELS ALIVE

  • 6 top leagues and their second divisions — promotion, relegation, and over 100 clubs.

  • Transfer windows with real negotiation drama: offers arrive, wait, and get withdrawn.

  • Contracts, wage talks and boardroom meetings. Earn your coach's trust week by week.

  • European competitions with a league phase, knockout rounds and finals.

  • A real season calendar on your wall — match by match, week by week.

YOUR ROOM IS YOUR HUB

Everything happens in your own room, on real objects:

  • A cork board with hand-pinned league standings and fixture notes.

  • A green chalkboard that runs your matchday — play or simulate, your call.

  • A retro 90s desktop computer: stats, transfer offers, social media, and decades of league history in the archive.

  • A magazine on the desk: your collection, your deck, and the market between its pages.

  • A trophy shelf that slowly fills, and a shirt on the wall for every club you've played for.

  • A training ground with card puzzles to sharpen your skills.

THE WORLD REACTS TO YOU

  • A living social media feed: fans celebrate you, mock you, and turn on you when form dips.

  • Press rumors, transfer gossip, title race hysteria and end-of-season verdicts.

  • A market value graph that rises and falls with your real performances.

Start as a nobody. Retire as a legend. Or don't — that part is up to your cards.

Play it alone or with friends.

A co-op incremental game for one to four players. You start in a tiny clearing in the middle of solid rock, with no gravity and no map. Throw a ball and it bounces, carving a tunnel until the rock stops it. Then throw another.

Four players, one cave. Invite friends, or hand anyone your cave code. Friends can drop into a cave that's already running, and each of you throws at your own pace.

Nothing slows a throw down here but the rock. Every ball keeps flying until its hits run out.

The Splitterball splits into three. The Lance drills a dead-straight tunnel. The Charge blows a hole in the wall. The Rot Ball rots the rock from the inside, the Arc Ball zaps everything near it, and the Magnet pulls your other balls to where it lands. Then pick how to throw them: a Single Shot, a Spread, a Twin back to back, a Broadside wall of shot, or a Sentry that keeps firing on its own.

Everything you mine rattles down a pachinko board, and where it lands decides what it pays. Crates buried in the rock hold the upgrades for the machine, and crates buried deeper out hold richer ones.

Hundreds of upgrades, on a map covered in fog. Buy one and its neighbours light up.

Four stones are buried out in the dark. Break a pair and a line points the way. Break all four and the one golden piece wakes up. Deep out there, crystal shatters in a ripple from a single hit, and ringing metal shrugs off everything but your special balls.

Also in the game

  • Online co-op for four players through Steam

  • Mouse and keyboard, or the whole game on a controller

  • 14 interface languages

  • Colour-blind mode and larger text

  • Five save slots, and you can keep digging after you win

Search a hand-drawn Peruvian-inspired finca for 850+ hidden cuys — adorable guinea pigs — plus snackos, keys, secrets, and suspiciously crunchy clues in a cozy hidden object adventure about the legendary Golden Corn.

A cozy hidden object snack hunt full of tiny squeaks

The cuys were perfectly happy nibbling grass outside the old finca.

Then they heard a rumor.

Somewhere inside the hacienda lies the legendary Golden Corn — a snack so glorious, so mysterious, so dangerously crunchy, that no guinea pig could possibly ignore it.

So begins a tiny, fluffy, deeply unreasonable expedition through Casa de Cuy.

What you will find

  • Find 850+ hidden cuys across 24+ hand-drawn areas

  • Collect snackos and use them to reveal hidden cuys

  • Unlock new paths, keys, doors, and secret places

  • Discover hidden extras, tiny puzzles, and suspiciously crunchy secrets

  • Follow a lighthearted story about the legendary Golden Corn

  • Enjoy hand-drawn artwork with soft, calming colors

  • Relax with a Peruvian-inspired instrumental soundtrack

  • Play at your own pace with mouse or controller

Search the finca, find the cuys, follow the crumbs

Explore 24+ hand-drawn areas filled with hidden guinea pigs, strange little details, secret corners, suspicious furniture, and snack-related chaos.

From sunny gardens, quiet rooms, and cozy balconies to dusty corners, hidden passages, strange old chambers, and places no guinea pig should ever enter, every area hides something worth finding — or at least something a cuy thought was edible.

Open doors. Unlock new areas. Find keys. Collect snackos. Follow clues. And keep an eye out for cuys hiding exactly where no responsible guinea pig should be.

A warm hand-drawn world full of tiny surprises

Casa de Cuy is a calm, cozy hidden object adventure with a playful hand-drawn line-art style and soft touches of color. Every area is packed with small visual jokes, cute details, hidden extras, and tiny surprises designed for players who enjoy looking closely and discovering things at their own pace.

It is silly, relaxing, family-friendly, and just mysterious enough to make you wonder what the cuys are really up to.

A tiny mystery with very fluffy suspects

The deeper you search, the stranger the finca becomes. Why are the cuys everywhere? Who started the Golden Corn rumor? Why does every locked door lead to even more squeaking?

There is only one way to find out.

Look closely. Trust no cushion. Follow the crumbs.



The Golden Corn awaits.

This is a visual novel game where players step into the shoes of a charismatic young man, building emotional connections through thoughtful choices. Your decisions directly influence affection levels, shaping your romantic interactions and delivering an engaging romance experience.

Game Features:

- Rich storyline with 30+ hours of uninterrupted gameplay

- Over 200 beautifully crafted animated CG cutscenes

- More than 20 romanceable female characters

- Make dialogue choices to increase affinity and unlock hidden animations

- Collect key items to unlock hidden animations

- Discover items to unlock new maps

- Classic QTE (Quick Time Event) gameplay

Characters

Emily: A young female college student and Mia’s junior at university. She is from Kaohsiung and has just moved north for college, leaving her hometown and family for the first time. She is quiet, introverted, reserved, and somewhat shy around strangers. She is innocent and straightforward rather than calculating, and she tends to smile when she talks. As she becomes more familiar with her surroundings, she gradually relaxes and opens up. Her main goal is to adapt to university life after leaving home for the first time and build new social relationships.

Lily: A young woman in her early twenties who runs a small family hair salon while also taking on the roles of homemaker and young mother. She is originally from the coastal area of Chiayi and later married into a family in Taipei, where she lives with her husband’s family. Her husband is two years younger than her, is currently twenty-one, and is serving in the military in Kinmen. They have a four-month-old baby. Her family situation is complicated, as she has to run the hair salon while caring for her child. She is polite and soft-spoken, with a distinct southern Chiayi accent and intonation. She is courteous toward unfamiliar customers, but becomes nervous, shy, and easily flustered when faced with family pressure or unexpected situations involving strangers. Her personal goal is to take good care of her baby, maintain her family life, and keep the hair salon running while hoping to get through everyday life steadily while her husband is away.

Mrs. Hu: An adult woman and middle-aged homemaker who is the landlady of the apartment where Ethan and several other students live. She is Mr. Hu’s wife, the mother of their children, and **Ruby’s** sister-in-law. Warm, talkative, and fond of entertaining guests, she has strong social skills and enjoys singing and drinking. She is quite familiar with the students living upstairs. Her personal goal is to enjoy family life during the winter break, spend time with relatives and friends, and maintain the familiar, friendly relationship between her family and her tenants.

Mia: A young female college student. She is Ethan’s senior at university as well as Emily’s senior. She has a boyfriend and lives in the same apartment building as Ethan. Outgoing, proactive, warm, and highly conversational, Mia is good at finding things to talk about and enjoys observing the relationships between people around her. She especially likes playing matchmaker and actively tries to bring Ethan and Emily together. Her main goal is to help the two of them meet and gradually become closer.

Grace: An adult woman who works at a university library. She is married, and her husband is her long-term and stable family partner. She usually comes across as kind, conservative, dignified, and approachable. She takes her work seriously and is accustomed to quietly organizing and shelving books in the library. She has a soft, full-figured adult build that clearly reflects an ordinary mature woman rather than a young student’s physique. She has short hair, a fair complexion, and normally wears only light makeup. Her main goal is to complete her library duties, maintain a peaceful and stable life, and preserve her identity within her family. However, when confronted with sudden attention or unexpected emotional stimulation, she may reveal vulnerability and inner conflict that have accumulated after being overlooked for a long time.

Ashley: A woman around twenty years old and a college student who is Ethan’s classmate. Outgoing, fashionable, confident, and lively, Ashley is highly social and enjoys being the visual center of attention. She is bold and direct, with a distinctly playful and teasing personality. She is well aware of her physical attractiveness and enjoys watching how people around her react to her. Her main motivation is to enjoy the social life of young adulthood, interactions with friends, and new and exciting experiences.

A retro-terminal detective game. Crack cases, analyze evidence, unmask a conspiracy.

Step into the chair of an FDI forensic data analyst. Case Analyst is an investigative OS-sim where you crack cases from a retro CRT terminal -- issuing commands, analyzing evidence, and staying in contact with your field agent as a branching story unfolds.

INVESTIGATE LIKE A PRO

- Drive a living terminal: scan, decrypt, trace, hack and more

- Examine photos and video in the Forensic Analyzer: find hidden hotspots, enhance details, read server logs and classified documents

- Coordinate with your field agent over an encrypted Field Link, where your choices shape the case

A STORY IN THREE ACTS

- 21 missions across 3 campaigns, from a routine first day to a sprawling conspiracy

- Branching decisions and tense, timed operations

- Three difficulty modes, from guided hints to fully redacted intel

Fully playable in English and Italian.

You are the dealer.

Every card leaves your hand, every payout is your call — and every mistake goes on your record.

Casino Dealer Simulator flips the casino game on its head: instead of playing against the house, you ARE the house. Clock in for a real-time shift at a 7-seat blackjack or Texas Hold'em table full of AI patrons with personalities, bankrolls, tempers and drinking habits — then deal, settle and survive.

DEAL EVERY CARD YOURSELF

Tap the felt in the right order, flip the hole card, draw to the house rules. No auto-pilot in Pro and Career modes: miscount a payout and the patron walks, the pit boss calls, and the difference comes out of your tips.

RUN TWO GAMES

Blackjack is your bread and butter; hold'em is where dealers earn their stripes. Rotate the button, burn and turn by hand, read every five-card hand at showdown, break the pot into side pots and push each stack to its rightful winner — a missed split pot is on you, and the shorted player will let the whole floor know.

READ THE TABLE

30+ hand-crafted voxel patrons rotate through your seats: cheap regulars, glamorous whales, a mafia don who tips in hundreds, a celebrity who bets against him out of spite. They order drinks, go on tilt, get impatient when you stall — and some of them cheat.

CATCH THE CHEATS

At the blackjack table, any regular can secretly start counting cards — their play goes suspiciously perfect. At hold'em, two patrons may quietly play as one team: never raising each other, squeezing everyone caught between them. Yours is the only eye that will notice. Report them to the pit boss — but be sure. Dragging an innocent patron off the floor costs you dearly.

CLIMB THE CAREER

Guaranteed shift salary plus grade bonuses (S to F), a 5-star reputation ladder from Trainee to Pit Boss, permanent achievements, and a persistent leaderboard. Earn 3 stars and you move upstairs: a marble VIP room with a grey-felt table and the casino's richest clientele.

NO REAL GAMBLING

Simulated casino money only. No real-money wagering, no microtransactions, no loot boxes. Just you, the shoe, and a floor manager with very little patience.

The old races made a pact in the dark: the age of man ends here. Every castle along the border has fallen. Yours is the last one standing, and thirteen armies are already on the road.

Castellan is a real-time roguelite castle defense where nothing plays itself. You aim every arrow, place every soldier and time every spell, all at once, while the horde keeps coming.

You are the castle

Hold the left mouse button and arrows fly wherever you point. You choose the target: the healer hiding behind the line, the rock thrower standing far from your walls, the supply chest falling from the sky. Press F to switch on auto fire and just aim. When the castle's health runs low, Last Stand begins: you shoot faster, your soldiers move faster and every kill pays more mastery. Some of the best comebacks start there.

Your soldiers are cards

Before each attempt you spend your gold on chests. Every card that comes out is a soldier in your squad for that attempt. In battle those cards sit in your hand: drag one onto the field and the soldier appears right where you dropped it. Put footmen in the gap, archers behind them and a cleric close enough to heal both. Changed your mind? Right-click a soldier to pick it up and move it.

There are 33 different soldiers in three roles: melee, ranged and healers. Each one brings its own trick. Lightning that jumps between enemies, shots that slow, blows that hit a whole group, extra damage against flying enemies, finishing off the wounded, war drums that speed up everyone nearby.

Nine spells, four slots

Spells come out of chests too, and you take four of them into battle on keys 1 to 4. Entangling Roots holds a wave in place. Frost Field slows it. Fireball burns it. Poison Cloud eats through it. Repair Ritual patches the castle, Sunburst punishes summoned enemies and Windshear drags flying enemies down to the ground. Rally Horn shields your whole army and brings back the last soldier you lost. Judgement takes a bite out of the strongest enemy on the field. Charges are limited, so every cast is a decision.

Lose, upgrade, return

Losing is part of the game. Every attempt pays mastery, even a failed one, and mastery buys upgrades that stay with you for good. There are 204 of them in 11 tabs: Castle Defense, Arrows, Supply Drops, Soldiers, Economy, Remnants, Overall Power, Spells, Chests & Cards, Elite & Boss, Advanced.

Tougher walls and castle repairs. More arrows per shot, critical hits, arrows that pierce. Stronger and faster soldiers. Supply chests that fall from the sky in the middle of a battle: shoot one open and its card flies straight into your hand. Stronger spells, luckier chests and special tools against elites and bosses.

Every chapter has five quests. Completing them raises your gold cap for good, which means more chests and a bigger army on the next attempt. Enemies you kill leave remnants that drift back to your castle. Upgrade them and they repair the walls, pay mastery and gold, or explode.

Thirteen chapters, thirteen rules to learn

Every chapter is a different army with its own elite, its own boss and its own rule. There are 85 different enemies in total, and brute force alone will not get you through:

  • Goblins that pour in like a flood while their slingers shoot over your front line.

  • Wolf clans that jump over your soldiers and land right at your walls.

  • Swamp witches that heal their army as fast as you hurt it.

  • Giants that stop far from your walls and throw rocks at your soldiers and your castle.

  • Skeletons that stand back up unless someone breaks the bone pile.

  • Vampires that turn your own soldiers against you.

  • A bronze bull that turns red just before it charges.

  • Gates that open in the middle of your field.

  • Wyverns that never land, and a dragon that only comes down when her brood is dead.

  • And at the end of the road, the pact itself, calling back every race and every boss you thought you had beaten.

Know what you are getting

Castellan is a single-player game played with the mouse and a handful of keys. It is a roguelite: a chapter is meant to take a few attempts, and every attempt leaves you stronger than the last. If you like learning an enemy, coming back with a better plan and finally breaking through, this is your kind of game.

At a glance

  • Real-time castle defense: you aim, deploy and cast yourself

  • 13 chapters, each with its own army, elite and boss

  • 85 different enemies with mechanics you have to answer

  • 33 different soldier cards: melee, ranged and healers

  • 9 spells, 4 slots, limited charges

  • 204 permanent upgrades in 11 tabs

  • 65 quests that raise your gold cap

  • A Collection that fills up as you open chests

  • Auto fire for long sessions

  • Playable in 15 languages

  • An indie game made by a solo developer

Every round you look after two things: your castle and your army.

The castle stays home. A wall stands in front of it, and behind it you build up five buildings: a cannon that fires on attackers, a treasury, a forge, a war banner and a witch's cauldron. Each time one of them levels up, you choose one of three upgrades.

The army goes out. When the build phase ends, it meets a rival's army in the field, and the winner marches on the loser's castle.

Put too much into the castle and your army falls behind. Put too much into the army and the next siege hurts more than it should. Most of the decisions in a match come back to that.

Units, items and heroes

  • 44 units across five rarities. Merge duplicates to level them up.
  • The forge turns iron into items. You pay, look at three and keep one. Every unit has four slots: head, chest, feet and weapon.
  • XP books level a unit up without needing a second copy. You get them from the banner and from treasure chests.
  • At the start of the match you pick one of six heroes. Each one pulls your game in a different direction.

Synergies

Seven races and eight classes. The class decides what a unit does in a fight: warriors make enemies bleed, mages burn or chill them, hexers curse them and rangers mark targets for everyone else. Races help the whole group, each in its own way, from fast beasts to undead that leave skeletons behind. Your army only has so many slots, so sooner or later a good unit ends up on the bench because it doesn't fit.

How a match plays out

  • The first three rounds are against monsters. After that you mostly fight other players.
  • Treasure rounds put two armies on one field, with no walls and no castles. The last side standing opens the chest.
  • A boss shows up every tenth round. Beat it and pick one of three power-ups that your army keeps for the rest of the match.
  • From round 51 on, attackers get stronger every round until only one castle is left.
Your castle's health is your life total, and it doesn't come back between rounds. A broken wall stays broken too, until you pay stone to fix it.

2 to 8 players, or solo

Everyone builds at the same time, so nobody sits around waiting for their turn. Online it's a free-for-all with up to eight players.

Solo you play against AI that sticks to the same rules you do: no extra gold, no stat bonuses, no looking at your board. The four difficulty levels change how well it plays, and each opponent has one of six play styles, from early rushers to economy players. There's also no clock: the fight starts when you end your turn.

At a glance

  • 44 units, 77 items, 6 heroes, 5 castle buildings
  • 7 races and 8 classes
  • Online free-for-all for 2 to 8 players, solo against AI on 4 difficulty levels
  • English, German, Spanish, Portuguese, Russian and Simplified Chinese

About This Game

Speak your spells. Explore ever-changing dungeons. Survive together.

Caster Crew is a 1–4 player co-op action roguelike where your voice becomes your most powerful weapon. Venture into procedurally generated dungeons, discover magical scrolls, collect valuable loot, and cast spells by speaking their incantations aloud.

Every expedition brings a different combination of rooms, enemies, treasures, and encounters. Coordinate with your party, manage your resources, and decide which spells and items will give you the best chance of reaching the next boss.

But knowing a spell is not enough—you must speak it when it matters.

Cast Magic With Your Voice

Equip magical scrolls and pronounce their incantations to activate your abilities. Each spell has its own command, effect, mana cost, and cooldown.

Stay calm during battle, choose the right spell, and make your voice heard before the dungeon overwhelms your party.

Procedurally Generated Expeditions

Each run assembles the dungeon from a variety of rooms and encounters. Explore changing layouts, search for hidden rewards, open treasure chests, and prepare for the dangers waiting beyond the next doorway.

The dungeon is generated from a shared seed, ensuring that every member of the party experiences the same adventure.

Fight Together

Play alone or form an online party of up to four players. Combine different spells, help teammates survive difficult encounters, and communicate through in-game voice chat as you explore.

Your party may share the same objective, but every player manages their own equipment, resources, and magical loadout.

Build Your Arsenal

Discover magical scrolls, weapons, consumables, and other useful items throughout each expedition. Treasure chests offer different levels of rarity and specialized rewards, encouraging you to adapt your build to what you find.

Between stages, visit the merchant to spend your personal share of the party’s earnings, improve your loadout, and prepare for the next part of the journey.

Face Multi-Phase Bosses

At the end of each dungeon waits a powerful boss encounter. Some bosses may transform, summon another form, or introduce entirely new threats as the battle progresses.

Defeat every phase, gather your rewards, and continue deeper into the run.

Key Features

  • Online co-op for 1–4 players

  • Voice-controlled spellcasting

  • Procedurally generated dungeon layouts

  • A variety of spells, weapons, consumables, and magical items

  • Weighted room, enemy, and treasure generation

  • Adaptive treasure rarity

Catadel: Slot Defense is a medieval slot-defense roguelite where you pull the lever, send an army of cats charging at the enemy, and pay your taxes. Match unit symbols, stack formations and let the cascades run to build up damage. That damage becomes Gold, making powerful combinations both your weapon and your income.

Invest now or save for tax day?

Each week brings two enemies, a boss, and then the royal tax. Gold pays for your bets, for food at the market and for restocking the shop, and for the tax: in full, on the day it is due. Defeating enemies is only part of survival. Come up short and the run ends, however well you fought. Every Gold piece you stake is a choice between security now and the chance to earn more later.

Limited spins. Bigger possibilities.

Every battle gives you only so many spins. Make the most of formations and cascading matches to push your damage and earnings higher, and win with spins to spare to earn extra Crowns. Royal Decrees, relics and supplies change what each spin can deliver.

Push your luck on the wheel

Your attack is ready. Strike now and keep it, or call ×2, ×5 or ×10 and spin the multiplier wheel. Land on your call and the attack is multiplied. Miss, and that attack is lost.

Bet on what remains

Before a spin, open the bet slip and call up to ten tiles, predicting for each one which unit will be left on it once every cascade has settled. Every call has its own odds, and the slip multiplies them together, up to ×1,000. Your Gold stake is deducted when you confirm and, once you spin, is not returned. If every call is right, your stake times the combined odds is added as bonus attack. Miss even one, and this spin’s attack and combat Gold are 0. The safest choice is not always the most profitable one.

Bets use only Gold earned in battle. No real money is ever involved.

Shape your strategy with decrees and treasures

Choose Royal Decrees and spend your Crowns in the market on relics, one-use supplies and upgrades. Increase the appearance rate of particular unit types, strengthen formation multipliers, or boost your cascades. Discover combinations that turn stronger attacks into greater income.

Even defenders need a break

Spinning nonstop can get a little dull, can’t it? Buy bread, sausage and butter at the market, slice and fry them in your carriage kitchen, and take a bite. Eating gives no combat bonus; it is simply a good lunch. Then pour a beer and take a moment to breathe. Of course, having one while you spin works too!

None of these rewards can be purchased for power; they are earned through progression, achievements, and dedication.

THE ARENA DOES NOT LIE

When you enter the Arena, cosmetics stay at the door. Your avatar, frame, and title provide absolutely no combat advantage, meaning they grant no additional damage, defense, or power. Every match is governed by the same rules, and every fight is validated by the server. Every item, every drop, every piece of gold, and every combat interaction is verified server-side, ensuring that the client is never trusted. There are no shortcuts and no pay-to-win advantages. In the Arena, your cosmetics cannot save you, your purchases cannot give you an advantage, and your status means nothing. The only things that matter are your character, your decisions, your build, and the skill of the player controlling it.

THE WAR HAS BEGUN

Champions of Thaloria is being forged by Idanthyr Studios. The city still stands, the ancient darkness is awakening, and the three bloodlines are preparing for a war unlike anything Thaloria has faced before. Beyond the walls, something that was supposed to remain dead is returning, while inside the city, old rivalries threaten to destroy the fragile alliance that has kept humanity alive for generations. Thaloria has survived for centuries, but survival is no longer guaranteed. The world is ready, the war has begun, and now it is time to decide whether you will stand with Thaloria.

You know chess.

Every capture becomes a battle. Your knight may charge a pawn expecting an easy victory—and never return. Every decision carries weight. Strength matters, experience matters, and sometimes the battlefield has other plans.

Chaos Chess takes the familiar rules of chess and builds an RPG strategy game around them, where every match leaves its mark on your army.

Every Battle Forges Your Army

Your pieces are more than disposable units.

Survive battles, gain experience, and turn ordinary soldiers into veterans and heroes. Develop powerful traits, shape your army over time, and create a force with its own history of victories, defeats, and unlikely survivors.

A pawn that should have fallen ten battles ago might become one of your greatest legends. Shape its story and follow its deeds across the battlefield.

Four Custom Campaigns

Chaos Chess features four distinct single-player campaigns, each built around its own mechanics and story.

Lead human forces through a war for the throne. Defend the Dwarven Heartforge as enemies close in. Explore a corrupted wasteland with the Legion in search of a lost totem. Rule the Dark Elves through choices, alliances, and battles where earlier decisions shape what happens later. All four explore chess from a new perspective.

These are not simply strings of chess matches. Each campaign approaches Chaos Chess in a different way.

Eight Armies — So Far

Take command of a growing roster of fantasy armies, each with its own identity, characters, and battlefield style.

Humans, outlaws, dwarves, dark elves, the Legion, and more bring their own personalities to the board, turning every matchup into a clash between very different forces.

Take Chaos Worldwide

Challenge other players online and put your army to the test.

Fight competitive PvP battles, climb the ranks, and discover whether the heroes who carried you through countless victories can survive against another player’s army.

Chess, With Consequences

At its heart, Chaos Chess is still chess.

Positioning matters. Tactics matter. Sacrifices matter.

But when two pieces collide, the result is no longer predetermined.

Every move is a decision.

Every capture is a battle.

Every army tells a story.

Chaos Cinema

Take over a run-down cinema and bring it back to life step by step.

Welcome to Chaos Cinema, a first-person cinema management game where you take over an old, neglected movie theater and try to turn it into a successful business again.

At the beginning, your cinema is dirty, damaged and only partially operational. Clean it up, remove old and broken elements, restock your stations and prepare everything for your first customers.

Sell tickets, purchase movie licenses and schedule your screenings. Run the concession counter, fill drinks, prepare popcorn and nachos, add flavors and extras, and assemble the correct orders for your customers.

But daily operations do not always go according to plan.

Drinks can spill, popcorn ends up on the floor, customers lose their patience and supplies run out exactly when the lobby is full. Machines and stations need to be refilled, trash needs to be removed, counters need to be cleaned and bathrooms need to be kept in order.

Your guests react to waiting time, accuracy, cleanliness, movies and ambience. Their ratings become visible during their visit and influence how successful your cinema becomes in the long run.

Every day is a balancing act between service, time pressure, cleanliness, supplies, movie scheduling and money. Earn enough to order new stock, improve your cinema and gradually turn a run-down building into a well-running movie theater.

Features

First-Person Cinema Management
Work directly inside your cinema. Sell tickets, run the concession counter, clean up, restock supplies and handle the daily operation yourself.

Hands-On Snack Service
Grab cups and containers directly from your stations, fill drinks, prepare popcorn and nachos, and assemble complete customer orders on the counter.

Flavors and Extras
Orders can include different sizes, flavors and add-ons. Pay close attention to exactly what your customers ordered.

Tickets and Movie Scheduling
Sell tickets, purchase movie licenses and plan when your movies will play in your auditorium.

Customers With Visible Reactions
Customers react to waiting times, incorrect orders, cleanliness, movies and service. Their ratings become visible during their visit.

Countdown to Showtime
Your guests want tickets and snacks, but the movie will not wait. Serve them in time before the screening begins.

Stock and Supply Management
Order supplies for your stations and storage area. Cups, popcorn, sauces, candy, drinks and other consumables need regular restocking.

Cleaning and Chaos System
Spilled drinks, popcorn on the floor, trash, dirty counters and messy bathrooms are all part of the job. Different types of mess require different cleaning methods.

Renovate Your Cinema
Your cinema starts in rough shape. Remove old and broken elements, clean everything up and improve the building step by step.

Ratings and End-of-Day Results
Speed, accuracy, cleanliness, movies and ambience influence your guests' opinions and the overall rating of your cinema.

Stylized Low-Poly Look
A colorful and playful visual style creates a charming and easy-to-read atmosphere.

Character Abyss is a turn-based card game. At its core are character tiles and character combination mechanics, with skills and enemies built around them, plus a combat system using Essence, Qi and Spirit as its base stats.

Venture deep into the mystic realm, make your choices, wield character tiles, and battle foes.

  • Character Tile Synthesis — Combine character tiles into words or short phrases to trigger unique effects.

  • Turn-based Combat — Build your deck, manage resources, and play cards whose powers derive from the original meanings of Chinese characters.

  • Light Roguelike Exploration — Enemies and events are procedurally generated.

  • Multiple Classes — Scholar synthesizes on the fly mid-combat; Talismanist pre-crafts powerful talismans.

  • Meta-Progression — Stronghold workshops, codex collection, and cross-run unlocks.

Want an Engineer who can revive pieces back? Or a Rook that can move 1 square diagonally? Maybe a Pawn that can also go backwards?

Well you got all of that in Checkmade.

Checkmade is still chess. Same board. Same checkmate. Same feeling that you should have seen that coming three moves ago. 

What changes is the army. You get a point budget, a piece limit, and a pile of blueprints — classic pieces, fairy movers, siege junk, kings that do more than sit in the corner. You build a loadout, take it into a match, and find out whether the theory holds up.

No loot ladders. No pay-to-win pieces. Tokens you earn in play unlock the roster and a few board skins. The rest is sitting with the board until something clicks.

Army Lab

Drag owned pieces onto the board. Watch the budget. Save the ones that feel right.

Every piece shows its move diagram, the actual rules in plain language, and a short scrap of lore if you care about that kind of thing. Some revive allies. Some explode on contact. Some just sit there and make three squares in front of them miserable for the enemy. You will put two pieces together that look brilliant and lose to a pawn that learned to step backward.

The roster

Start with the familiar set if you want. Or don't.

Open Chaos Packs with tokens you earn from matches. Commons stack up. Rares and better show up often enough that the collection doesn't feel like a second job. Pity on every pack: at least one Rare or better. Stack caps keep things from getting silly.

War Machines. Sappers. Hot Cauldrons. Engineers who treat the dead like reusable timber. If it has a legal move pattern and fits the budget, it can end up on your back row.

Match

  • Play against AI across a range of difficulties, including ones that will make you doubt your life choices.

  • Local hotseat when someone is sitting next to you.

  • Quick Random if you want a loadout and a fight without opening the Lab first.

  • Play Online by launching the online version. Quick matchmaking or invite code style.

Click a piece, read what it actually does, then move. Illegal attempts get told off. The board does not care about your plan.

Puzzles

Mate in one, two, or three. Built-in challenges to learn the odd pieces without burning a whole match.

There is also a Puzzle Designer: place pieces, set the mate depth, playtest until it is honest, then save it. Publish to the Workshop when you are ready to hand your trap to strangers.

Skin Lab

Board skins and piece presentation, unlocked with the same tokens. Preview before you commit. Classic wood, neon circuit, rune stone — or stick with the original and get back to the game.

If that sounds like you

Checkmade is for people who like chess enough to argue about it, and variants enough to open a spreadsheet. Build an army. Break a few habits. Lose to Nightmare. Open one more pack. Try again.

Checkmate is not traditional Chinese chess. It is a cannon-blazing roguelite fought across a 9×10 battlefield.

Take control of Red’s last General and survive an overwhelming enemy army. Move, brace your cannon, reload and fire. Use enemy pieces as cannon screens, calculate each blast radius, and choose between the risk of a scattered quick shot and the precision of an aimed attack.

Every Action Advances the Battle

Moving, firing and upgrading all give the enemy another chance to act. Chariots, horses, cannons and soldiers close in according to their own rules—and a single mistake may leave your General with no escape.

Power Always Has a Price

Choose cards that improve your firepower, range, ammunition and special tactics. At the same time, the enemy gains new abilities, units and rule changes. The stronger your build becomes, the more dangerous the board grows.

Fight Your Way Out

  • Turn-based tactical combat on a 9×10 board

  • Cannon fire, aimed attacks, reloading and melee combat

  • Extensive card builds and rule combinations

  • Evolving enemy armies and mounting endgame pressure

  • Multiple piece skins and achievement challenges

  • A single-player campaign and endless challenges

Break through the encirclement, blast open the palace and bring down the enemy General.

CHESS ARMY

In chess, a sacrificed piece never returns. Chess Army takes that lesson to heart.

It is a tactical turn-based roguelike. Your units are not chess pieces: they are soldiers, mages, cavalry, and spearmen. However, each one moves according to the patterns of a chess piece. But here, death is permanent: a fallen unit does not rise again. You have only one action per turn, and if your commander dies, the campaign ends with them.

Four army corps, four ways to move

Every unit belongs to one of four army corps, and its corps decides how it crosses the battlefield. Mages move on the diagonal, like the bishop: they strike from afar, but never in a straight line. Cavalry vaults over units in an L, like the knight. Spearmen and guards advance and strike in straight lines, like the rook, and lock down the lanes. Infantry, meanwhile, moves in all eight directions like the queen: the most versatile corps, the backbone your whole army rests on.

An army born from your victories

You start with almost nothing. After every battle you recruit one of the last three enemies you cut down, and your army is built, quite literally, from what you destroy. Stash reinforcements in reserve, then, before the next fight, fuse three identical pawns to evolve them. Every base class opens two paths, each leading to two specialisations: 28 playable classes in all. A plain soldier can end up a raging barbarian or a weapon master; a mage, a protective archbishop or a warlock that feeds on its targets' blood. You sculpt your army, one battle at a time.

Three phases. Eighteen battles. Three warlords.

A campaign runs across three phases of six missions each. Skirmishes to thin the ranks, a special mission at the heart of every phase, and a boss to close it out. Each phase throws a different warlord at you, each with a style of its own, and the deeper you go, the harder the one waiting for you hits. Only the last one seals your victory.

Every tile matters

Terrain isn't decoration. A bush reduces the damage you take, a boulder blocks the line of sight, water reshapes every path. With each unit's own traits in play, a good position soon beats a good piece.

Equip, command, risk it all

Chests hide equipment (common, rare, legendary), and each unit can carry one. At the head of your army stands a commander, one you pick from several, each with its own command tree that reshapes a whole run's strategy. Between battles, spend your command points across that tree: sharpen your leader, harden your troops, or expand your logistics to deploy and keep more units. And keep your nerve: your commander is the one piece that can't be replaced.

In short

  • Turn-based tactical combat on a grid, in pixel art

  • Four army corps (infantry, mages, cavalry, spearmen), each moving like a chess piece

  • Roguelike recruitment: your army grows from defeated foes

  • 28 playable classes, unlocked by fusing your pawns

  • 18 battles, 3 phases, a different boss at the end of each

  • Each unit can carry a piece of equipment (common, rare, legendary)

  • Several commanders, each with its own command tree that reshapes a run's strategy

  • Terrain, line of sight, and a host of traits that reward positioning

  • Permadeath: the run ends with your commander

Build your army, set your pieces, and lead your commander all the way to the final boss.

YOUR NEXT MOVE STARTS HERE

Chess Town is a cozy chess career simulation where every move matters — on and off the board.

Build your strategy, make difficult decisions during tense matches, rise through local tournaments, and shape a life around the game you love. Your path to becoming a stronger player is not decided by chess alone.

Chess is more than finding a good move.

During matches, choose decision cards that shape your approach to the position. Anticipate your opponent’s plans, combine tactics, react to dangerous threats, and commit to the line that best fits your strategy.

The pieces follow the logic of chess — but your decisions determine the plan behind every move.

  • Build tactical momentum through smart card choices

  • Read your opponent’s intentions and answer their threats

  • Create powerful combinations at the right moment

  • Turn a difficult position into a memorable victory

Step into the Tournament Hall and put your preparation to the test.

Enter events, follow the standings, face new opponents, and fight your way through every round. A strong result can move you closer to the next stage of your chess career — but every tournament demands focus, preparation, and nerve.

  • Compete in local chess tournaments

  • Follow rankings and tournament progress

  • Face new opponents as your career develops

  • Chase the next title, prize, and breakthrough

A chess career needs more than ambition.

Take on construction work, react to fast-paced challenges, manage risk, and earn the money you need to keep pursuing your goals. Every job is another step toward supporting your career in Chess Town.

  • Take on hands-on construction jobs

  • React quickly to changing work conditions

  • Balance risk and reward

  • Earn money to support your chess career

When time is short, every second counts.

Pick up urgent deliveries, race through the streets of Chess Town, and earn what you need before the clock runs out. The city keeps moving — and so does your career.

  • Take urgent courier shifts

  • Race against the clock

  • Earn money through quick deliveries

  • Make every day count

YOUR CAREER. YOUR PLAN. YOUR NEXT MOVE.

From the local chess club to the pressure of the Tournament Hall, every day brings a new decision.

Build your life, sharpen your strategy, and see how far your chess career can go in Chess Town.

Chess You is an interactive chess game where you play against a cast of unique girls.

The game follows the standard rules of chess—no special gimmicks, just classic chess.

Each girl has her own personality and skill level.

They tease you, laugh at you, complain, and provoke you throughout the match.

Different personalities, different ways of thinking—

but they all share one thing in common:

They all want to play chess with You.

One deck. One board. And an endgame nobody has finished in three thousand years.

Chess of the Hidden Gates is a roguelike deckbuilder that runs on Chinese chess footwork. Every card in your hand is a move, and every move decides who gets taken.

Beyond numbers: position

Nobody stands still trading damage here. A beast’s blade lands on a square, not on your health bar: step aside and the hit means nothing, stand in the wrong spot and you’re surrounded. Read the board, bait your enemies, force the position you want. Your strongest card played from the wrong square still loses. What wins here is the chess.

Three pieces, three ways to play

  • Horse Master — build Momentum on the move, throw spears that stay on the board, then call every one of them back through whatever stands in the way.

  • Pawn Commander — every square you hold turns into armor. Go Steadfast and nothing shifts you.

  • Cannon Adept — fire through a piece in the way, and Relay shots carry all the way across the board.

Bring friends to the board

The full game supports online co-op for 2–3 players. Invite one or two Steam friends to share a run on one board, all playing in the same turn. Will you trip up your teammate's horse, or step in front and take the hit for them?

A teammate can be the screen your cannon fires through, and a Horse Master's spears stay on the board for anyone to pick up and throw again. More players, more beasts with more health. There are also over twenty co-op-only cards.

The world is a board; all things are pieces

The battle of Zhuolu never ended. Its endgame is still sitting there, locked behind the Eight Gates, and you are the last player to walk in. You bring one deck, and every card in it moves a piece. The knight leaps, the cannon fires through a screen, the pawn crosses the river and never turns back. Your deck is how you move, and how you move is what keeps you alive.

What’s on the board

  • Over 300 cards across four rarities — each one a move, a kill, or a trap.

  • Three classes, three signature systems: Momentum burst, Steadfast defense, Relay artillery.

  • Over forty beasts, each with a backstory, a temper, and a mechanic of its own.

  • Nine Star bosses across three acts, each one rewriting the rules, all the way up to Chiyou at the end.

  • Reshuffled every run: terrain, threats, beasts, drops. No two runs inside the Eight Gates are alike.

  • A living bestiary: beat a beast and you unlock its story, written up like pages from an old field journal.

Every enemy is a prisoner

The beasts in these mountains are prisoners of a thousand-year-old board. The wolves are the grudges of Zhuolu’s fallen soldiers; the foxes are a corrupted line of the sacred Qingqiu; the tree blocking your path was planted to seal this prison and has guarded the gate ever since. Over forty creatures, each with a history, a temper, and a habit of punishing you for not reading the board. Past the last gate, the Nine Stars rotate every run: a false healer who patches up every lesser beast, a fire-star that burns the whole board through, and Tianfu, the fallen sage, who turns your own class’s cards against you. Fight all the way to the end and what is left of Chiyou is waiting, along with a choice.

Prisoners can change sides

Land the killing blow with a Spirit Seal and the beast turns into a card in your deck. Summon it back and it fights for you, with its own health, damage and temper intact. Fifty-one of them, one for nearly every creature on the board, the Nine Stars included. The board that locks them up is also how you let them out.

One table, one duel

The whole war fits on one scholar’s desk: a lacquered board for a battlefield, carved figurines for pieces, incense and candlelight around the edges. You lean over it the way you’d lean over a real game, and a three-thousand-year endgame starts moving again under your hand.

The hero fights. You decide.

Chest & Blade runs its own combat. Your hero clears a stage, moves to the next one, and casts equipped active skills as they come off cooldown. You are not clicking every hit — you are deciding what to change when a stage stops going down.



  • Each act ends with a boss that gates the way forward.
  • Loot Chests, Treasure Chests and Dragon Chests drop gear from Common all the way up to Mythic.
  • Offline progress keeps collecting rewards while the game is closed, up to an 8-hour cap.

Choose Your Hero

Create a character, pick a class, set how they look, and send them out.
Warrior — Hold the front line behind your shield and bring Blade Rain down on the whole wave. The steadiest way to start.



Mage — Stay back and let Chain Lightning leap from enemy to enemy. Fragile, but every point of Intelligence turns into damage.



Barbarian — Roll back, cut through the whole line with Blood Wave and drink back the damage you deal. Heavy axe, no mercy.



Every class has its own skill list and its own stat scaling, so a second character is a different run rather than the same one again.

Hunt for Better Gear

Most of the game sits in what you equip. Rarity does not only raise the numbers — it decides how many affixes an item rolls, so two legendary swords can point at two completely different builds.



  • Weapons are class-bound; armor and accessories are open to any hero.
  • Affixes roll from stat families in fixed tiers: damage, crit, attack speed, health, gold and drop rate, and more.
  • Slot upgrades are permanent. The plus sits on the equipment slot instead of the item, so it survives every gear swap.

The Forge is where gear stops being random

  • Salvage what you do not need. Scrap is not a consolation prize, it is the economy.
  • Combine three items of the same rarity into one of the next, and craft from recipes.
  • Reroll affixes when a piece is almost right.

Shape Your Build

  • Skills — spend skill points across your class tree of passives, actives and an ultimate. Equipped actives fire automatically in combat, by priority.
  • Runes — a wide board of long-term bonuses across several branches, funded mostly with gold, so farming always has somewhere to go.
  • Augments — every few levels you draft one of three cards, which makes a level-up a decision instead of an automatic stat bump.



Break the Wall, Push Further

  • Daily and weekly quests hand you short goals to clear next to whatever stage you are pushing.
  • Tiered achievements track the long haul: kills, chests opened, rarities found.
  • Clear the final act and Heroic opens up — the same world on a much harder curve, with your progress intact.
  • There is no prestige reset waiting to take your progress away.
Fight, loot, forge, adjust, push one act further. If you like idle games where the screen keeps working but the build still matters, that is the loop Chest & Blade is built around.

Loot Chests


Venture deep into the dungeon and loot a wide variety of chests, uncovering increasingly rare and powerful cards.

Open Card Packs


Open the card packs you've collected. Every card grants a permanent boost to your power, making you stronger with every pack.

Keep Growing


Cards aren't the only way to grow. Unlock multiple progression systems to continuously increase your strength, discover higher-tier card packs, and take on even greater challenges.

You want to play football. Your parents want good grades. Your coach wants results. The club would like to see your paperwork first.

China Youth Academy combines a young player's coming-of-age story with grassroots club management in a world of football and dark comedy. Live three formative years in a child's pursuit of a dream, or take charge of an academy with three squads depending on you. There is the joy of scoring a goal, and the less celebrated challenge of getting one form approved.

#### 01 | Twelve Years Old. A Chance Still to Earn.

Begin in the summer after primary school. Choose your talents, flaws and path through school football, community training, a professional academy or a sports school. Balance study, training and rest, seek your family's support and attend trials. Time and money are limited. Your future depends on more than your attributes: it depends on how you spend your days.

#### 02 | Looking Good in Training Is Not the Same as Playing Well

Work on your fundamentals and fitness, or explore stranger routines, including football calisthenics and the fine art of standing with your hands on your hips. Different approaches bring different benefits and trade-offs. Better stamina may come with clumsier footwork; a well-practised pose may at least improve your composure. The match will test what your training record is really worth.

#### 03 | Your Decision. Your Moment.

Matches unfold in real time, pausing at key moments for you to choose between three actions. Take on a defender, make the pass or risk something bolder? Movement, challenges, fouls, offside and set pieces shape the contest. Watch your chosen action play out and become part of the match record. You are competing for more than a goal: you are earning the chance to be trusted again.

#### 04 | Some of the Toughest Defences Are Off the Pitch

How do you ask for training money or explain slipping grades? Can you earn the trust of your coach and teammates? Conversations at home, at school and around the team let you argue your case, use humour or compromise, with consequences for your relationships. Football may be your dream, but the people helping you pursue it have hopes of their own.

#### 05 | One News Story a Day. Business as Unusual.

Daily youth-football news brings sudden announcements, public controversies and impressive-sounding statements into your routine. Repeat the official line, question the facts or stay silent: your response can affect reputation, relationships and public pressure. Sometimes the hardest call of the day is not offside. It is working out what a notice actually means.

#### 06 | Before You Play, Read the Contract

Training fees, registration requirements, transfer conditions and the cost of leaving can turn an opportunity into another obstacle. Clubs, parents and intermediaries may tell very different stories about the same offer. Decide which promises deserve your trust and which terms demand a closer look. Your signature may shape how much freedom you have later.

#### 07 | Take Charge of the Academy

Club-management mode puts you in charge of U13, U16 and U19 squads. Recruit players and coaches, plan training and tactics, manage lineups and injuries, and balance wages, fees and transfers while competing in city leagues and national tournaments. Rivals keep recruiting. Parents keep negotiating. Your budget does not grow simply because you love the game.

#### 08 | More Than One Future. More Than One Kind of Success.

Pursue a place in a professional academy, aim for the youth national team or find another balance between education and football. Your choices lead to different endings, with story illustrations, achievements and career records marking the path you took. After three years, will you be closer to your original dream, or will you have found a different answer?

Football is never just about winning. But a real chance to step onto the pitch is still worth fighting for.

### Fictional Content Notice

The game's cities, clubs, characters, competition organisers and stories are fictional. Its portrayal of institutions and industry practices uses exaggeration and satire and is not intended to depict specific real-world organisations or individuals.

Take Over the Franchise

Stop screaming at your screen, “I could coach better than this fraud.”
Fine. Keyboard’s yours, coach.

You are now in charge of everything: building the roster, running practices, managing egos, fixing the locker room vibes, drawing up ATOs on the whiteboard, and doing dark CBA wizardry just to survive the luxury tax. Your mission is simple: build a team so broken that your grandma could three-peat with it.

Run Your 12-Man Roster

Manage your 12-man squad and try not to get cooked by the salary cap. Find value in the vet-minimum bargain bin, avoid locking yourself into cap hell, and pray your max-contract superstar does not become a load-management merchant the second the ink dries.

Watch out for certified contract-year frauds, washed allegations, fake tough guys, and players whose only elite skill is clapping from the bench. But do not disrespect the end-of-bench towel GOAT either. Every dynasty needs a guy who gives you elite vibes per 36.

A Real Player Ecosystem

This is not just “click train, numbers go up.”
You have to manage development, injuries, chemistry, morale, ego, and body-language-per-possession.

One bad week and your star is on fraud watch. One ugly loss and the nephews are posting lowlights with captions like “legacy points deducted.” Then suddenly someone throws an elbow, someone else hits a “totally natural shooting motion” directly into another man’s future bloodline, and now your rotation is in shambles.
